review_comments: I think we should not generate an arrow function from here, as we apply `arrow` before `parameters`.

A little bit context is needed. As discussed in #3268, Safari somehow still has bug for parameters until today(swc have `safari_id_destructuring_collision_in_function_expression` to fix it), so even if class properties is supported, a parameters pass is still needed. So this is only for Safari > 14.1 and `bugfixes: false`, where arrow function is supported perfectly.

[Babel](https://babeljs.io/repl#?browsers=safari%2014.1&build=&builtIns=false&corejs=3.6&spec=true&loose=false&code_lz=MYGwhgzhAECC0G8BQ1pmgXmgRmgamgApCA6MsASkwD40KVoAjTIskxqjW5ggFwAsAljAYReYXoODRpWQrJwAmAMyda0vkJEBfIA&debug=false&forceAllTransforms=false&shippedProposals=false&circleciRepo=&evaluate=false&fileSize=true&timeTravel=false&sourceType=module&lineWrap=true&presets=env&prettier=false&targets=&version=7.17.2&externalPlugins=&assumptions=%7B%7D) behaves the same(you need to mannually close bugfixes), and there's no other way to capture `this` in class field

But as this pass is applied after arrow, the emitted code will not work in browsers that only support es5.
I'm not talking about browers with support for arrows.
For browser that doesn't support arrows, there's no chance they support class field, so this shall still work, but implicit dependency between passes is indeed a bad thing.

Oh, I see.
My bad, sorry. I tried creating some example and found that class properties will not exist in ast in such cases. Thanks!
